items.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997
items.q: This was in the ‘55 band... I was with them for seven years. It was Al Porcino... really some swing players.

ctx.x: Yeah, I mean he’d walk, he was like six foot seven, he walked out on stage, and I mean but he gave you that look when he walked out on stage, like he had, I mean he’d spread his arms and he’d cover the front of the orchestra.

I’ll tell you a story about the swinging thing. This was in the ‘55 band, that was about the swingingest band that I ever was on with Kenton, I was with them for seven years. It was Al Porcino, and you know, really some swing players. We were in New York, we had a night off, so Al Porcino, who’s got that voice, I don’t know if you know who he is, but anyway, he said, “Count Basie’s band is down at Birdland. I think everyone should go down and listen to Count Basie.” So we all did, but not because he said it, but…
